title: Small units, giant chains
question: How do small molecules become materials as different as plastic, rubber and DNA?
hook: A bag of plastic, a rubber band and your own DNA are all built by chaining small pieces together.
idea: Polymers are large molecules made of many repeating units, and they can be natural or synthetic.

beats.prompt: Sort each polymer into its group.
beats.explain: Polymers are of two types, naturally occurring and synthetic or man made.

beats.prompt: Match each term to what it means.
pairs: A small molecule that links up to build a polymer
Combining many monomers into a bonded chain or network
The piece of each monomer incorporated into the polymer
beats.explain: Monomers are the small molecules, polymerization is the process, and the repeat unit is the part of each monomer that ends up in the chain.

beats.prompt: One step in this reasoning is wrong. Which?
steps: PET polyester is made from terephthalic acid and ethylene glycol.
Its repeating unit corresponds to the two monomers combined, with two water molecules lost.
So the repeat unit must contain every atom of both monomers.
The piece of each monomer that is incorporated is called the repeat unit.
beats.explain: Two water molecules are lost, so the repeat unit does not contain every atom of both monomers.

beats.prompt: A chemist heats natural rubber in the presence of sulfur. What forms?

choices.label: Nitrocellulose
choices.feedback: It tempts because it is also made from a natural polymer, but it comes from reacting nitric acid with cellulose.

choices.label: A silicone
choices.feedback: Silicones have silicon in the backbone, so they are not made by heating rubber with sulfur.

choices.label: Polystyrene
choices.feedback: It is a synthetic polymer built from monomers, not made by modifying natural rubber.

beats.explain: Vulcanized rubber forms by heating natural rubber in the presence of sulfur.
